text:
Emilia: Quick follow-up from today's runtime all-hands. A few concrete asks from GTM/PMs: (a) exact canary window for kernel-v4, (b) what telemetry will be available to product for latency/cost comparisons, and (c) short guidance on fallback behaviour we can paste into the roadmap doc.

Ryan: Canary window = 2 weeks starting 2025-06-01 (canary pool only). Roll to broader Dedicated/Hosted depends on canary signals; tentative broader push mid-June if no regressions.

Aisha: Telemetry scope: per-kernel latency histograms (p50/p90/p95/p99), per-seq-length and per-batch-size buckets, kv-cache hit/miss ratios, and memory growth over 1m/5m/1h windows. We'll also expose an aggregated cost-per-token estimate (tokens * kernel_cost_factor). We'll add a product-facing dashboard tile.

Mark: For PMs: fallback routing behaviour is rule-driven. If kernel variant fails healthchecks or crosses error rate threshold, traffic is moved to the next compatible variant in the route list. It is deterministic and logged in the Console routing timeline. Short snippet you can paste: "Routing: automatic fallback to healthy variant; can be pinned in Console; audit log available."

Tash: Performance tips to include in the doc: microbatching reduces tail latency for interactive workloads. For v4 I've seen best median latency at microbatch=8-16 for 512-seq on 80G; throughput gains reappear at batch>=64 on multi-GPU. Also note v4 allocates larger transient KV buffers on long sequences; recommend enabling kv-cache-evict policy for session-based workloads.

Victor: Will the kernel histograms be per-tenant or only aggregated? Concerned about noisy p99 spikes from small tenants.

Aisha: We'll publish both aggregated and per-tenant (opt-in) histograms. For alerting we'll use tenant-aware thresholds and a rolling-median filter to damp transient spikes.

Emilia: Any immediate operational mitigations if canary shows memory pressure? We need a rapid action plan to communicate.

Ryan: Ops playbook: 1) reduce default batch_size for affected pools, 2) switch traffic from v4 to v3 variants for heavy tails, 3) increase node eviction thresholds temporarily, 4) roll a config patch disabling KV prefetch. We'll script the first two for quick toggles.

ops-bot: [alert] 2025-06-02T02:14 - Canary pool memory anomaly detected; auto-scaled and diverted 12% traffic to fallback variants.

Aisha: Investigating root cause: early indicator points to transient KV reallocs in attention kernel when sequence >2048. Patch path: reduce prealloctable slab and short-circuit empty KV writes. Target patch ETA: 36-48 hours; canary retest after patch.

Mark: I'll prepare the PM 1-pager with: kernel variants table (expected p50/p95/p99 ranges), recommended microbatch sizes, cost-per-token estimates, and routing/fallback summary. Will post a draft here by EOD.

Tash: I'll publish a short perf appendix with example curl commands and the microbench harness outputs so PMs can reproduce numbers locally. Example: `./bench --model kernel-v4 --seq 512 --batch 16` plus CSV.

Emilia: Great. Action items recap: Aisha = telemetry endpoints + patch ETA; Ryan = ops quick toggles + playbook; Mark = PM 1-pager; Tash = perf appendix + bench commands. Please drop links here when ready.

Victor: One last ask: can we add an explicit note in the roadmap about "expected behavior under memory pressure" so customers don't misinterpret rollbacks as reliability issues?

Ryan: Yes — we'll add a short note explaining automated fallback, why it happens (protect nodes & latency), and where to find audit logs.

Emilia: Thanks everyone. Ping back with links. :white_check_mark:
